END_REVOLUTION_DESC.en: Despite your efforts, the day of the Revolution came faster than anybody had anticipated. A battalion of armed commoners stormed the gates of the capital, catching the nobles by surprise. Most of the army turned a blind eye - the rest could hardly stand against a force with nothing to lose. A lucky few nobles managed to flee in the commotion, but the rest were dragged out into the streets and slain as the mob approached your palace. There was nothing you could do, nobody you could turn to. The revolutionaries broke down your door, poured into your estate, and finally, cornered you in your room. You barely had the chance to utter a word before you were struck down. As you fell to the floor, you chanced a look outside your balcony window and saw the flag of the revolt rising in the smoky morning sky. The reign of the monarchy had come to an end.

END_COMMON_ASSASSIN_DESC.en: While you weren't looking, from the crowd, a shot rang out. An instant later, you felt the pain in your chest. Evidently, you had angered the commoners enough that somebody had dared to lay down their life to kill you. The gunman was tackled to the floor, but it was too late. Screams echoed around you as panic ensued. Or perhaps they were cheers...? You couldn't say. You were rushed to the hospital, but it was far too late. Without your rule, your kingdom would descend into chaos. If you were lucky, perhaps the nobles or revolutionaries could restore order. If not... well, it wasn't your problem anymore, at least. Regardless, your reign had come to an end.

END_NOBLE_ASSASSIN_DESC.en: Late at night, as you returned to your chambers, you thought you saw a shadowy figure dart out of sight in the corner of your eye. You turned to look, but you could see nothing... until, suddenly, a flash of light. A shot rang out, and a sharp pain flooded your body. Instantly you crumpled to the floor. As you writhed in agony, you heard cold, even footsteps approaching you. You mustered up the courage to meet the eyes of your assassin, only to see a familiar face: one of your own nobles, face twisted into a wicked grin. They raised the still-smoking gun up toward your head, and before you could even dare to ask why, they fired a second shot to finish the job. Your death would no doubt be written off as a tragic accident, or perhaps the work of the rebels. No matter how much power you believed you had, in the end, disappointing your nobles had proved to be your undoing.

END_FLEE_DOCK_FAIL_DESC.en: Under cover of the night, you approached the misty coastline, ragged cloak covering your face. You carefully made your way down the shore, glancing to and fro in hopes of spotting your vessel. Unfortunately, somebody else spotted you first. A deafening shot caught your ear, and the bullet struck your leg, causing you to fall to the ground. As you attempted to crawl away, the gunman approached, flanked by none other than a fellow noble. A trap. It appeared that your "loyal followers" weren't exactly keen on letting you simply run away after all the problems you had caused them. Before you could beg for your life, a second bullet struck you, and you were tossed into the sea, never to be seen again.

END_FLEE_DOCK_SUCCESS_DESC.en: Under cover of the night, you fled your palace and made your way down to the misty coastline, with nothing but a few of your most precious belongings in tow. There, after a few moments of frantic searching, you spotted him: a lone sailor standing next to a small vessel, beckoning you toward him. You clambered aboard the vessel, and in a flash, the ship departed. It was a quiet journey, the sailor not daring to speak anything beyond a mumbled "I'm sorry" somewhere along the way. As the boat made its way into the port, you handed the sailor a generous stack of coins and made your way toward a waiting carriage, ready to bring you to the Winstonian palace where you would meet with your former equal. Here, you would not be a ruler, but you would surely be an esteemed guest of honor. Your nobles, while betrayed, didn't care enough to hunt you down before their inevitable demise at the hands of the rebels. The newly-democratic government of your old lands were willing to let you live so long as you never returned, which of course you didn't. You lived out the rest of your days in Winstone, spending your days quietly and peacefully... although murmurs from the Winstonian commoners speaking of democracy kept your hairs standing on end all the while.

END_FLEE_MINES_FAIL_DESC.en: Following the instructions given to you by the kindly Peasant Girl, you made your way in the dark of the night toward the mines, taking care not to lose your footing on the uneven terrain. As you climbed the hilly path and came into view of the supposed secret tunnel, however, you found it blocked by a mob of angry peasants. At first, you thought you had been betrayed - however, you then saw the Peasant Girl toward the head of the crowd, bound and gagged, struggling to warn you of the ambush. Somehow the miners had found out about your plot to escape, and they were none too pleased with you avoiding the consequences of your actions. You attempted to turn and run as they spotted you, but you slipped on the loose soil and fell to the ground. In an instant, you were surrounded by the rabble, and a cacophony of angry shouts erupted. It seemed they were unsure of what to do with you, but before you could even begin to beg for your life, some sort of sharp instrument dug itself into your side. The crowd began to dissolve into infighting, but those who wanted you dead were sure to deliver the killing blow before cooler heads could prevail. In the end, your body was buried deep inside the tunnel, and while your killers were eventually tried and executed by the nobility, your body would never be found.

END_FLEE_MINES_SUCCESS_DESC.en: Carrying little more than a few of your most valuable possessions and a few provisions given to you by the kind peasant family you had saved, you hurriedly made your way through the mines under cover of the night. As you made your way up the loose, barely-defined path of a nondescript hill, your destination finally came into view: a small cave entrance, hidden by tall grass. You carefully stepped inside to find that it was, indeed, a tunnel, and after what felt like hours of carefully making your way through the tight corridors, you finally saw the dim moonlight peek through the exit. You stepped outside to find yourself in the wilderness, but wilderness in lands far from your own. You rushed onward, following the stars, until you found what the Peasant Girl said should be your final destination: a foreign village, mostly farmers and other such humble folk. You laid low for a time, disguising yourself as a simple traveler and merchant, and the locals treated you well. The coins you had smuggled along certainly did you well. After a time, you planned to make your way to a larger city, but before you could, the news made its way to the village that the revolution had taken control of your old kingdom. Realizing the dangers of being recognized if you tried to meet with a fellow ruler, you decided to stay put, and eventually settled into your new humble life. It was far from glamorous, but you lived out the rest of your days in relative peace, making out a modest existence and making merry with people you would have once never paid a second thought to - all because you bothered to save the lives of one family.

END_FLEE_OUTSKIRTS_FAIL_DESC.en: On a cloudy, moonless night, laying in the back of a wagon carried along by a single horse and silent rider, you made your way along a dusty road. The Baron had given you some basic provisions and one last firm handshake before he sent you on your way, organizing a ride that would take you to a secret mountain pass. However, as you stared at the dark sky above, your wagon made a sudden halt, and your horse's rider let out a gasp. You raised your head to see what the fuss was about, only to find yourself suddenly surrounded by armed soldiers, their faces barely visible. You tried to ask what they were doing, only to be instantly struck town by the blade of a bayonet. As your horseman screamed in terror, you head a familiar voice congratulating your assailants on their efforts. It was one of your very own nobles. Evidently, someone had learned of your ambush, and wasn't exactly keen on letting you escape after you had wronged them. Had the Baron sold you out? Or was he to be killed, next? You would never know. Your body was tossed to the wolves, and you were never found.

END_FLEE_OUTSKIRTS_SUCCESS_DESC.en: On a cloudy, moonless night, you made your way along a dusty road, laying in the back of a wagon carried along by a single horse and silent rider. The Baron had arranged the ride for you, sending you off with a bag of provisions and one last firm handshake toward a secret mountain pass. The wheels creaked and your surroundings shook as you gazed into the dark sky, until finally, the wagon came to a stop at the edge of a small valley. You paid your rider handsomely before stepping out and beginning the long trek toward your destination. By the time you made your way through the pass, the sun had already begun to rise, and it was fully in the sky by the time you were approached by a pair of Bandalburger riders. They were suspicious at first, speaking in a language you only partly knew and pointing swords at your throat before you presented them with a letter from the Baron and a small stack of coins. Their faces lit up. You rode with them for several days, across fields and hills, until finally you came into sight of the Bandalburger capital. There, you were given an audience with the king. Hearing of your plight, and because of the peace you had negotiated, he agreed to shelter you as a guest of honor from any furious nobles or rebels. Before long, news arrived that the rebellion had taken control of your kingdom, but by then you had become close friends with the king, and ultimately you were allowed to stay. Slowly but surely you integrated into Bandalburger society, and while your life was never nearly as luxurious as it was back in your palace, your knowledge of your kingdom's forces kept your new home safe when war eventually erupted again. You never again were able to speak to the Baron, or if he even still lived, but you lived the rest of your life thanking him.

END_SURRENDER_FAIL_DESC.en: Seeing the writing on the wall and faced with a crowd of furious rebels, you decided to hand yourself over to your opponents, becoming their prisoner. You were promised your life if you came quietly, but as you spent your months in your dry, solemn prison cell, the murmurs and passing conversations you heard made it clear that the rebellion would not keep their word. One morning, two stern-looking armed guards stepped into your cell, demanding you come with them. They draped a cloth over your head and led you along for what felt like an eternity, the voices of a crowd growing louder and louder until your march was suddenly stopped. The veil over your head was lifted to reveal that you were now standing in front of a seemingly endless mob, as if you were giving a speech just like the olden days. But the wooden frame which surrounded you made clear that this was not the case. This was a gallows. You could barely hear the righteous raving of the rebel leader next to you as you tried to process what was going on, your head and hands being placed into a tight holder by your captors. As the blade above you was raised, the leader asked you to speak your last words. You couldn't choke up a single thought before the rope holding the blade was cut and your life came to a swift end. The revolution had won, but you had to wonder: how many more would be slain just like you?

END_SURRENDER_SUCCESS_DESC.en: Seeing the writing on the wall and faced with a crowd of furious rebels, you decided to hand yourself over to your opponents, becoming their prisoner. Being led to the very prison which had once held key rebel figures, you were promised you would be allowed to live, although you weren't quite so sure. Indeed, as you listened to the heated discussions echoing through the prison walls, it seemed as though there was quite a lot of disagreement about what to do with you. In the end, though, cooler heads prevailed, and the moderates who had come to head the new government decided that you did not deserve death. Your freedom, however, was another story. You spent the rest of your life inside the prison walls, slowly wasting away as time mached on. From your window, you saw great strife, celebrations, and periods of national mourning, but most of all, you saw slow and steady progress. You couldn't help but wonder to yourself whether that progress was because you were gone, and whether you truly had made the world worse with your mere existence, through endless, sleepless nights. But at least you were alive.

END_ABDICATE_FAIL_DESC.en: Faced with an overwhelming, angry crowd of rebels, you knew in an instant that your time as ruler had come to an end. But perhaps this end wouldn't have to come with strife. Gracefully, you stepped down, and after being allowed to speak with the leaders of the rebellion, you decreed a formal end to the monarchy. While many in the rebel ranks were furious at the idea of allowing you to live after what you had done, it was ultimately agreed that you would be allowed to live a quiet, peaceful life on a small estate far from your center of power, albeit with a watchful eye always kept over you. After the toll the rebellion had taken on you, though, this kind of quiet life was exactly what you wanted. Unfortunately, however, your retirement would be cut short. In the middle of the night, as you laid peacefully in your bed, you were startled awake by the sound of angry yelling and banging on the door. As you rose to your feet, you heard the door get smashed in, and then a stomping up the stairs. You shied into a corner as a pair of scowling gunmen made their way into the bedroom. You were quickly spotted and surrounded, and before you could even beg for your life, several shots rang out. You would never know whether the attack had come from a furious spurned noble or a radical faction of the rebellion taking justice into their own hands, and indeed, nobody else would, either. The debate over who killed you spilled over into the eact kind of violence you had hoped to avoid with your abdication, throwing your kingdom into years of turmoil you would never get to see.

END_ABDICATE_SUCCESS_DESC.en: Faced with an overwhelming, angry crowd of rebels, you knew in an instant that your time as ruler had come to an end. But perhaps this end wouldn't have to come with strife. Gracefully, you stepped down, and after speaking with the leaders of the rebellion, you decreed a formal end to the monarchy. In exchange, you were promised the ability to live out the rest of your life in peace in a modest estate on the outskirts of your former kingdom, albeit under constant surveillance. While some in the rebellion were unhappy with allowing you to live so freely, ultimately the government decided that clemency was the best solution, and the disagreements quieted down. Your nobles, too, were furious, but seeing as you had treated them so well, none ever bothered to seek revenge - a few were tried for their crimes and jailed, others fled, but quite a few made the transition into ordinary citizens. With some members of the elite still in power, the new rebel government struggled with corruption and power struggles, but none of this ever bothered you. After all the chaos you had endured, you were more than happy to live out the rest of your life in peace, away from whatever the future would bring to your people, good or bad.
